title: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption
body:
Read the chapter → [Jeremiah 32](/bible/jeremiah/32)

This session covers Jeremiah chapters 32 through 35 during the Babylonian captivity of the Israelites, a history also found in 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and the prophets Daniel and Ezekiel. While Jerusalem is besieged and Jeremiah is shut up in prison, the Most High commands him to buy a field as a sign that houses, fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again in the land after the seventy years. The reading moves through the prophecy of full restoration, the everlasting covenant and the branch of righteousness raised up to David, the broken covenant over the liberty of the servants, and the obedience of the Rechabites held up as a rebuke to Judah.

**[Jeremiah 32:1-5](/bible/jeremiah/32#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/jeremiah/32#v1)</sup> The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/jeremiah/32#v2)</sup> For then the king of Babylon’s army besieged Jerusalem: and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah’s house.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/jeremiah/32#v3)</sup> For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, Wherefore dost thou prophesy, and say, Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/jeremiah/32#v4)</sup> And Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes;
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/jeremiah/32#v5)</sup> And he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the Lord: though ye fight with the Chaldeans, ye shall not prosper.

- The word came to Jeremiah in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, when the king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem and Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison.
- Zedekiah had imprisoned him for prophesying that the Most High would give the city into the hand of the king of Babylon; Zedekiah himself would not escape but would be led to Babylon, speak with him mouth to mouth, and behold his eyes.
- This was the word of the Most High that came through Jeremiah to the king, that though they fight against the Chaldeans they should not prosper.

**[Jeremiah 32:6-12](/bible/jeremiah/32#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/jeremiah/32#v6)</sup> And Jeremiah said, The word of the Lord came unto me, saying,
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/jeremiah/32#v7)</sup> Behold, Hanameel the son of Shallum thine uncle shall come unto thee, saying, Buy thee my field that is in Anathoth: for the right of redemption is thine to buy it.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/jeremiah/32#v8)</sup> So Hanameel mine uncle’s son came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the Lord, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin: for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine; buy it for thyself. Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/jeremiah/32#v9)</sup> And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncle’s son, that was in Anathoth, and weighed him the money, even seventeen shekels of silver.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/jeremiah/32#v10)</sup> And I subscribed the evidence, and sealed it, and took witnesses, and weighed him the money in the balances.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/jeremiah/32#v11)</sup> So I took the evidence of the purchase, both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open:
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/jeremiah/32#v12)</sup> And I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the sight of Hanameel mine uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses that subscribed the book of the purchase, before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.

- Hanameel his uncle's son came to Jeremiah in the court of the prison to sell him the field at Anathoth, for the right of redemption and inheritance was Jeremiah's; then he knew it was the word of the Most High.
- He bought the field, weighed him seventeen shekels of silver, subscribed the evidence, sealed it, and took witnesses, taking both the sealed evidence and the open according to the law and custom, and delivered it to Baruch the son of Neriah.
- Anathoth was in the country of Benjamin because the priests were given cities and suburbs to dwell in.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 42:7](/bible/sirach/42#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/sirach/42#v7)</sup> Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.

    We are supposed to put all things in writing, for evidence is the only way to prove something.

**[Jeremiah 32:13-15](/bible/jeremiah/32#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/jeremiah/32#v13)</sup> And I charged Baruch before them, saying,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/jeremiah/32#v14)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both which is sealed, and this evidence which is open; and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/jeremiah/32#v15)</sup> For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.

- Jeremiah charged Baruch before the witnesses to take both the sealed and the open evidence of the purchase and put them in an earthen vessel that they might continue many days.
- The Most High declares that houses, fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land, because the prophecy was that the captivity would last seventy years and then the people would return.
  - **[Jeremiah 25:11](/bible/jeremiah/25#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/jeremiah/25#v11)</sup> And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

    The whole land would be a desolation and these nations serve the king of Babylon seventy years before He punished Babylon; after Babylon we passed to the Persians and Medes, and Cyrus the Persian let us return.

**[Jeremiah 32:16-25](/bible/jeremiah/32#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/jeremiah/32#v16)</sup> Now when I had delivered the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed unto the Lord, saying,
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/jeremiah/32#v17)</sup> Ah Lord God! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/jeremiah/32#v18)</sup> Thou shewest lovingkindness unto thousands, and recompensest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: the Great, the Mighty God, the Lord of hosts, is his name,
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/jeremiah/32#v19)</sup> Great in counsel, and mighty in work: for thine eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men: to give every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings:
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/jeremiah/32#v20)</sup> Which hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, even unto this day, and in Israel, and among other men; and hast made thee a name, as at this day;
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/32#v21)</sup> And hast brought forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror;
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/32#v22)</sup> And hast given them this land, which thou didst swear to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey;
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/jeremiah/32#v23)</sup> And they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do: therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/jeremiah/32#v24)</sup> Behold the mounts, they are come unto the city to take it; and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans, that fight against it, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence: and what thou hast spoken is come to pass; and, behold, thou seest it.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/jeremiah/32#v25)</sup> And thou hast said unto me, O Lord God, Buy thee the field for money, and take witnesses; for the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

- After delivering the evidence to Baruch, Jeremiah prayed, confessing that the Most High made heaven and earth by His great power and that nothing is too hard for Him.
- He is the great and mighty God, His eyes open upon all the ways of the sons of men to give everyone according to his ways, who brought Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders and gave them a land flowing with milk and honey.
- The people came in and possessed the land but obeyed not His voice nor walked in His law, therefore He caused all this evil to come upon them, even as the mounts came up against the city to take it.
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)</sup> But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee:

    The curses came because we came in and possessed the land but would not walk in the ways of the Most High as He commanded.

**[Jeremiah 32:26-35](/bible/jeremiah/32#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/jeremiah/32#v26)</sup> Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/jeremiah/32#v27)</sup> Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/jeremiah/32#v28)</sup> Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he shall take it:
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/jeremiah/32#v29)</sup> And the Chaldeans, that fight against this city, shall come and set fire on this city, and burn it with the houses, upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink offerings unto other gods, to provoke me to anger.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/jeremiah/32#v30)</sup> For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth: for the children of Israel have only provoked me to anger with the work of their hands, saith the Lord.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/jeremiah/32#v31)</sup> For this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face,
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/jeremiah/32#v32)</sup> Because of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/jeremiah/32#v33)</sup> And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/jeremiah/32#v34)</sup> But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/jeremiah/32#v35)</sup> And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.

- The Most High answers that He is the God of all flesh and nothing is too hard for Him; He will give the city into the hand of the Chaldeans and Nebuchadnezzar, who will set fire on it and burn it.
- On the same roofs where the people offered incense to Baal and poured drink offerings to other gods, He will have this people burn their houses to the ground for provoking Him to anger.
- The children of Israel and Judah, their kings, princes, priests, and prophets turned their backs to Him and not their faces, and set their abominations in the house called by His name to defile it.
- They built the high places of Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom to cause their sons and daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech, an abomination He never commanded.
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:25](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v25)**
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v25)</sup> The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.

    We were not to bring the abomination into our house, and definitely not into the house of the Most High to pollute it.

**[Jeremiah 32:36-41](/bible/jeremiah/32#v36)**

> <sup>[36](/bible/jeremiah/32#v36)</sup> And now therefore thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning this city, whereof ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence;
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/jeremiah/32#v37)</sup> Behold, I will gather them out of all countries, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely:
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/jeremiah/32#v38)</sup> And they shall be my people, and I will be their God:
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/jeremiah/32#v39)</sup> And I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for the good of them, and of their children after them:
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/jeremiah/32#v40)</sup> And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good; but I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/jeremiah/32#v41)</sup> Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul.

- Concerning the city they say is delivered to Babylon by sword, famine, and pestilence, the Most High will gather the people out of all countries where He drove them and bring them again to dwell safely, a prophecy of a time of redemption.
- He will give them one heart and one way, one mind and full agreement, and make an everlasting covenant with them, putting His fear in their hearts that they shall not depart from Him.
- This is being seen today as we rise up and get understanding of who we are, our nationality, and our God being a black God for His people, a God who does not love all nations alike but will reward these nations for what they have done to us.
  - **[John 14:6](/bible/john/14#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/john/14#v6)</sup> Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

    There are no multiple ways and no multiple truths; there is one way to the Father through the Son, which answers why Christianity has so many denominations.

**[Jeremiah 32:42-44](/bible/jeremiah/32#v42)**

> <sup>[42](/bible/jeremiah/32#v42)</sup> For thus saith the Lord; Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/jeremiah/32#v43)</sup> And fields shall be bought in this land, whereof ye say, It is desolate without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/jeremiah/32#v44)</sup> Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe evidences, and seal them, and take witnesses in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the south: for I will cause their captivity to return, saith the Lord.

- As He brought all this great evil, so the Most High will bring the good He has promised, and fields shall be bought again in the land men now say is desolate, with evidences subscribed, sealed, and witnessed.
- Fields will be bought in Benjamin, about Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, the mountains, the valley, and the south, for He will cause their captivity to return.
- After the Babylonian and Persian captivities the northern kingdom came to the western hemisphere, so these things, us all being set back in the land and in full agreement, have yet to take place.
  - **[Matthew 5:17-18](/bible/matthew/5#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/matthew/5#v17)</sup> Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/matthew/5#v18)</sup> For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.

    All things are not yet fulfilled, for we are still scattered and cannot rightly keep the high holy days in our enemies' lands.
